title: Demon's Catalyst
snippet:
Demon's Catalyst -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Demon's Catalyst is the second-heaviest catalyst in the game to the Manus Catalyst, which weighs one unit more. It has one of the lowest potential magic adjusts of any catalyst, being the lowest until 41 Intelligence where it surpasses the Oolacile Ivory Catalyst and Oolacile Catalyst. It trades these things for being a powerful melee weapon, dealing Fire and Thrust damage with its strong attack. The high strength and dexterity scaling will have a powerful effect on dark sorceries, as the physical damage dealt by those sorceries are boosted by those stats. Overall the Demon's Catalyst should be considered as a weapon that is effective with dark sorceries, but is not as effective with regular sorceries.

title: Affinity (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Affinity (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - spell - effect 
 effect : Conjures up five orbs around the caster, similar to Homing Soulmass. When an enemy within the caster's frontal arc gets close enough, the orbs lock on and slowly chase the target, with each orb capable of dealing 0.6 times the Spell Buff of the wielded catalyst as Dark damage upon impact. If the orbs collide with any level geometry without flying at a target, they will automatically explode.

As with other Dark Sorceries, this spell is subject to having its power boosted by wielding the proper catalyst.

Unlike Homing Soulmass and Homing Crystal Soulmass, the number of orbs conjured is always 5, regardless of the caster's Intelligence.

title: Affinity (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Affinity (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - spell - description 
 description : A forbidden dark sorcery. Casts a dark manifestation of humanity.

It appears to be an expression of envy, or perhaps love towards another, that will tenaciously pursue its target. Even if, like so many human desires, it amounts to nothing but misfortune.

title: Amana Shrine Maiden
snippet:
Amana Shrine Maiden -  Dark Souls II - enemy - strategy 
 strategy : Amana Shrine Maidens pose a large threat from a distance. There are some instances, however, where the player will be able to use a bow to snipe a Maiden without provoking them to attack. Even if the Shrine Maiden does aggro, they have no Poise so landing a successful hit on them will stagger them, interrupting their ability to cast.

Should the player get within melee range of a Maiden, she will pose little threat and fall in a few hits.

Poison can be used to effectively kill the Maidens as well. The player just needs to inflict the status effect on the Maidens, then get out of spell range and wait for the Maidens to die.

If they are knocked down (such as by the Smelter Hammer's spinning attack, or the Great Club's and Large Club's two-handed heavy attack) they will not stand up again.

title: Archdeacon's Great Staff
snippet: It should not be confused with the Crystal Chime, which can cast Sorceries and Miracles based on leveling Intelligence and Faith equally, or the Izalith Staff, which is designed for Dark Sorceries. The Golden Ritual Spear is a hybrid weapon that can also function as a staff, and operates on the same principle as the Archdeacon's Great Staff. The Man-grub's Staff is another staff that scales off of a stat that is not Intelligence.

title: Archdeacon's Great Staff
snippet:
Archdeacon's Great Staff -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Although it is a staff, the Archdeacon's Great Staff scales purely off of Faith rather than Intelligence. As such, it is designed to be used by builds with high amounts of Faith and utility amounts of Intelligence. Although this requires a high investment in levels into multiple stats, the benefit is that it allows high Faith builds to cast Sorceries with power on par with their Miracles. This allows it to be utilized on very unconventional builds, as both Lightning Stake and Great Heavy Soul Arrow can be cast on the same character to devastating effect.

However it is outclassed by the Bone Staff when it comes to Hexer builds, which has better scaling in Dark, and can be found at around the same point in the game, if not earlier.

A mediocre staff that can serve Hexers well in the early game, especially if they want to use a combination of Sorceries and Hexes. However, it is easily surpassed by other staves available later in the game.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

While the **Assassin** doesn't have any ranged attack, its Spook Sorcery is extremely useful for removing most non-fatal fall damage and for completely silencing footsteps for 20 seconds, allowing certain obstacles to be bypassed . Unfortunately, while the starting Sorcerer's Staff is a fairly good spell tool, if not exactly the best, it won't actually start to gain scaling from stats until Intelligence has reached at least 19, delaying a possible strengthening of the character's Sorceries.

Picking up the Soul Arrow Sorcery from the Shrine Handmaid gives a reusable ranged attack early on, while the weapon buffing Magic Weapon Sorcery can be gained in either Undead Settlement or Road of Sacrifices to add some of a Staff's spellbuff to weapon damage.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Assassin** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 3*.

It is a Dexterity-based class with decent Attunement for Weapon Arts and spells and some Intelligence for Sorceries.

An unusually long Thrusting Sword, the Estoc is also quite strong and has a rare sweeping heavy attack for hitting several or agile foes easier, at the cost of not having an increased critical modifier for Ripostes and Backstabs. Additionally, its Weapon Art, Shield Splitter, helps with its bad damage to the stamina of blocking targets by partially bypassing the defences of the block instead.

Its Targeting Shield, while not very suitable for blocking, is one of the game's three parrying shields and as such its Parry starts slightly earlier yet ends as late as the regular parry.

The Assassin Set has only moderate physical defences but has good magic and fire defences, and high overall resistances against anything that isn't Bleed.

title: Assassin (class)
snippet:
Assassin (class) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - trivia 
 trivia : This class is fairly popular amongst speedrunners thanks to Spook making it possible to easier skip foes and falls.
While the Assassin doesn't have any direct equivalent class in the Dark Souls series, it does bear some resemblance to the Royalty class from FromSoftware's previous game Demon's Souls, another Dexterity/Intelligence-based class wielding a thrusting sword (in that case a Rapier) and a small shield while also providing access to a Sorcery-like spell (though in the Royalty's case it is the offensive Soul Arrow, not a self-buffing spell).

title: Attunement (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Attunement (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Attunement** is a stat in *Dark Souls III* that increases the player character's Focus Points, or FP as well as increasing the number of Attunement slots.

Focus Points are used to cast Sorceries, Pyromancies and Miracles, as well as performing skills.

Spells can be attuned at the bonfire, provided the player has available Attunement slots. A minimum investment of 10 Attunement is required for one Attunement slot.

As it is with every other stat in the game, it also has indirect bonuses such as increasing the player character's flat defenses.

Leveling Attunement provides the following benefits:

Diminishing returns for increasing the amount of FP begin at 35 Attunement, while every 10 Attunement past 30 (except at 80 Attunement) will grant an additional slot. Equipping any one of the Saint's Ring, Deep Ring and Darkmoon Ring will grant 1, 1 and 2 additional Attunement slots, respectively.

title: Attunement (Dark Souls III)

title: Azal's Staff
snippet:
Azal's Staff -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Azal's Staff is a staff of extremes. It lowers the player's spell uses by 75% rounding down, has very slow casting speed (only the Chime of Screams is slower), and is extremely fragile, exhausting it's mere 4 durability with just a few casts. However, it has an S scaling in both Magic and Dark, allowing for a maximum increase of 540 for both elements in scaling damage and an effect that increases damage by 2.5%.

Bracing Knuckle Ring, Repair, Repair Powder and Clear Bluestone Ring, can help to combat this staff's debilitating downsides, though unless the player has an use for having extreme scaling in *both* Magic and Dark, a specialized staff such as Staff of Wisdom or Sunset Staff will generally serve much better.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bandit (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bandit** is one of the classes in *Dark Souls 2*.

It has high Dexterity and well above average Faith, meaning it lends itself rather well towards builds focused either on both or only the former (though it will have strong competition from the Swordsman when it comes to pure Dexterity builds). It is rather unsuitable to spells, even the Miracle ones, due to its extremely low Attunement and Intelligence.

Bandits are actually unable to speak to Straid of Olaphis by default, the only class that can't do that, due to its extremely low Intelligence not meeting his minimum required amount of 3.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet: There is a curious disadvantage to its high Vitality, higher than any other starting class: when using the Third Dragon Ring, it cannot receive the full benefit of the Flynn's Ring and will get a light decrease of 4 Attack Rating compared to any other class.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Until an unlimited source of arrows is acquired, they are best either saved for trying to pull individual enemies from groups or ambushes, or for trying to kill one of the early Ogres (either the one outside the Firekeeper's Hut in Things Betwixt at the start of the tutorial that also holds the Stone Ring, or the Scholar of the First Sin-exclusive one on the way towards the Forest of Fallen Giants) for a large amount of extra Souls.

The class's Bandit Set is actually fairly good, as it has somewhat high physical defences and is, together with the Knight's partial Falconer Set, the only starting set with decent starting Poise.

Due to its very low Adaptability and Attunement it has a substandard roll (only 7 i-frames, compared to most other classes having 8 or 9 i-frames) and needs 3 points in Adaptability or 9 points in Attunement to improve this to 8 i-frames.

title: Bandit (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Bandits are actually unable to speak to Straid of Olaphis by default, the only class that can't do that, due to its extremely low Intelligence not meeting his minimum required amount of 3.

The starting weapons are somewhat mixed, with the Short Bow following the higher starting value in Dexterity while the Hand Axe instead focuses on Strength. The Hand Axe is most likely better replaced with an actually Dexterity-focused weapon, though those are in limited supply until Blacksmith Lenigrast's shop is opened, mostly the Dagger in Things Betwixt and the Halberd in the Forest of Fallen Giants. Beyond extra weapons such as the Spear and the Rapier, Lenigrast also holds the game's first infinite supply of ammunition (merely more Wood Arrows, but still) and another Short Bow.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - lead 
 lead : is a character in *Dark Souls*. First met in Sen's Fortress, from which he relocates to Firelink Shrine, he is a merchant of advanced sorceries, including new ones upon following his questline into The Duke's Archives.

Voiced by Ian Thompson in his final role before his passing in 2022, Logan is also a mentioned character in *Dark Souls II* and a mentioned character in *Dark Souls III*, although *Dark Souls II* refers to him as an unnamed "master sorcerer" due to his name being forgotten in Drangleic.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Master Logan was a famous Sorcerer and a royal member of the Vinheim Dragon School before he turned Undead about one hundred years ago. His nickname stems from the gigantic hat he wore which completely hid his face; he used it to block the noise and stares from those around him in order to focus his thoughts. His weapon was once an ordinary catalyst employed by the Sorcerers of Vinheim, but it has since been strengthened due to lengthy use over time. His sage robe, called prototype, meaning it goes back the School foundation of the Dragon School, therefore the School was founded around the times Logan was alive.

Logan is credited with having developed the Soul Spear Sorcery, among others, which is referenced repeatedly in the legends and is said to be on par with Lord Gwyn's lightning.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
Big Hat Logan -  Dark Souls - character - trivia 
 trivia : Big Hat Logan seems to prefer sitting down in a meditative position, except for the first encounter when he's in a hanging jail cage.
If you get the Man-Serpent leaning against the wall next to the cage he is in, It will break, meaning you don't need to get the boulder trap to break it, with careful planning.
Logan shares many similarities with Sage Freke from *Demon's Souls*. Both are first found trapped in cages and rescued by the player. Both are preceded by apprentices looking for them, have an unhealthy fascination with magic, and are found sitting in the main hub area.
Rickert of Vinheim mentions to the player that Big Hat Logan is famous in Vinheim; however, he also mentions that Logan was from "a hundred years ago". Either Logan has remained sane for as long as he has been undead, or time warping in Lordran has brought Logan to a time where one does not belong.

title: Big Hat Logan
snippet:
When Logan is encountered hostile, he is not hollowed, but was driven insane in a more "traditional" sense. All other NPCs appear in their charred, undead forms when they attack players after hollowing.
If the player dies fighting against Big Hat Logan while in Seath's arena, the player will respawn in the prison as if they were killed by Seath himself, which underlines that Logan became just as mad as Seath.
Logan's Tin Crystallization Catalyst is actually 結晶の錫杖 ("Crystall Staff"). 錫杖 (khakkhara), is a ringed staff used by Buddhist monks. This implies that Logan venerated Seath as a God.

title: Sorcery (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Sorcery (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Sorceries are cast by catalysts. Catalysts scale with the Intelligence stat, with the unique exception of Tin Darkmoon Catalyst, which scales with Faith.

Most sorceries can be purchased from various merchants found throughout the game. Some are found as lootable items.

There are more sorceries than either pyromancies or miracles. While pyromancies focus on offensive spells and miracles focus on defensive and healing, sorceries include a variety of utility and augmentation spells as well as a range of offensive spells.

All forms of offensive sorceries cause Magic Damage, which is typically effective against iron armor, tough scales, and other physically resilient materials.

title: Spell Buff
snippet:
Spell Buff -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - basic_mechanics 
 basic_mechanics : The only thing that directly influences a catalyst's Spell Buff are the Faith/Intelligence of the player, and as such, when upgrading a catalyst, the scaling of these stats will rise and so will its overall Spell Buff. The higher the level of the wielder's Intelligence/Faith stats, the higher the numbers of Spell Buff on a given catalyst.

A catalyst has a base Spell Buff of 100, with additional Spell Buff being added on top of this value based on the scaling of the associated stat(s). If one or both stat requirements are not met, Spell Buff will be set to a flat value of 60 regardless of other circumstances.

title: Faith (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Faith (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Faith** is a stat in *Dark Souls III* that increases attack damage with Faith-based weapons and catalysts as well as increased damage output with spells such as Miracles and Pyromancies.

Faith increases damage done by weapons and catalysts through the use of a scaling mechanic. A letter denoting a weapons specific scaling properties is noted beneath the weapon's required faith stat. The letters range in order of effectiveness from **E**, **D**, **C**, **B**, **A**, and **S**.

Weapons and catalysts with an **E** rating for scaling will receive a poor benefit from investment in faith while weapons with an **S** rating receive the greatest benefit.

Note: the term **Catalyst** refers to any medium used to cast spells.

title: Spell Buff
snippet:
Catalysts that are fit to cast Dark Spells will continue to scale optimally up until 45 each of both Intelligence and Faith.

The Spell Buff of a Dark Catalyst scales equally with Intelligence and Faith. Provided that both stats are of equal level, each will provide half of the increased Spell Buff above 100. When used to cast Dark Spells (Gnaw, Great Deep Soul), both halves of the Spell Buff will be used to calculate its potency. However, when casting normal spells (Lightning Spear, Soul Spear), only the respective associated stat will be used to calculate Spell Buff, reducing the potency of the spell cast.

In the case of Crystal Chime, the inverse is true. Although Crystal Chime scales with both Intelligence and Faith, it is ill-suited for casting Dark Spells, and the results of attempting as such will yield severely weakened spells.

title: Intelligence (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Intelligence (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Intelligence** is a stat in *Dark Souls III* that increases attack damage with Intelligence-based weapons and catalysts as well as increased damage output with spells such as Sorceries and Pyromancies.

Intelligence increases damage done by weapons and catalysts through the use of a scaling mechanic. A letter denoting a weapons specific scaling properties is noted beneath the weapon's required intelligence stat. The letters range in order of effectiveness from **E**, **D**, **C**, **B**, **A**, and **S**.

Weapons and catalysts with an **E** rating for scaling will receive a poor benefit from investment in intelligence while weapons with an **S** rating receive the greatest benefit.

Note: the term **Catalyst** refers to any medium used to cast spells.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - elemental_damage 
 elemental_damage : Elemental damage scales off of one's Intelligence and Faith. The type of element will also affect which of the two stats is relevant, unless both are applied.

Elemental damage scales as follows:
Magic is usually affected by Intelligence, but can also on some occasions be affected by Faith. However, they're rarely mixed.
Fire is generally boosted by a combination of Intelligence and Faith, scaling equally well with both stats.
Lightning is always affected by Faith.
Dark is, much like fire, affected by both Intelligence and Faith, and scales equally well with both.

title: Faith (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Sacred Chimes and Talismans used for casting Miracles will see very strong returns from Faith investment. Almost all such catalysts require leveling Faith to a minimum of 18 before Spell Buff begins to increase, and this continues to improve the strength of the catalyst up until 60 Faith is reached. For most Faith catalysts, the rate of Spell Buff improvement falls off after 45 Faith.

For catalysts that specialize in casting Pyromancies, Dark Sorceries and Dark Miracles, the scaling and soft-caps behave differently. As like their melee counterparts, Pyromancy Flames will improve up until 40 Faith is reached, alongside 40 Intelligence. For specialized Dark catalysts like the Izalith Staff and Caitha's Chime, this cap is instead 45 Faith and 45 Intelligence. Crystal Chime also soft-caps at these values, however its scaling falls off noticeably past 30 Faith and 30 Intelligence.

title: Faith (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Faith (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - description 
 description : Faith is an attribute used to meet requirements for melee weapons, Talismans, and spells; Faith softcaps are **30/50**. Similar to Intelligence, the amount of damage you deal and the amount of HP you heal from healing based Miracles will correlate with the Talisman you are using rather than your overall point investment into Faith. Faith is also a weapon modifier, increasing magical damage for unique weapons (see Weapon Scaling) any weapon upgraded down the Divine or Occult paths. Faith also serves to boost your magic defense. You will want to meet but not exceed the requirements to use spells, weapons, and Talismans.

Faith also increases the lightning damage of the Dragonslayer Spear and the physical damage of the (cursed) Greatsword of Artorias.

title: Elemental Damage
snippet:
Elemental Damage -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : In *Dark Souls II*, a new elemental damage type in the form of Dark has been added, as well as the Hexes school of casting. All forms of elemental damage are tied to how Intelligence and Faith are leveled up, with different amounts of effectiveness depending on the stat spread. Magic is tied to Intelligence, Lightning is tied to Faith, while Fire is tied to the sum of both, and Dark is tied to the lower of both.

title: Spell (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Spell (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Spells are broken down into four classes: sorceries, miracles, pyromancies, and hexes.

Each spell type is cast with a catalyst: staves for sorcery, sacred chimes for miracles, pyromancy flames for pyromancy, and staves or sacred chimes for hexes. In addition, each spell type is associated with a magic type: Magic for sorcery, Lightning for miracles, Fire for pyromancy, and Dark for hexes.

Casting a spell sometimes necessitates meeting the minimum attribute requirements: Intelligence for sorceries, Faith for miracles, and a mixture of both Intelligence and Faith for hexes. Pyromancies are unique in that they have no attribute requirements to cast.

title: Izalith Staff
snippet: However, the flip side is that when casting Dark Sorceries such as Great Deep Soul, Spell Buff from Faith is accounted for, meaning that the staff's displayed Spell Buff is utilized to its fullest. Furthermore, Dark Sorceries cast from this staff benefit from an approximately 57% damage boost, greatly magnifying their damage output. Unlike the Murky Longstaff, the Izalith Staff scales strongly with both Intelligence and Faith, meaning that should the wielder be able to invest great amounts of points into both stats, the Izalith Staff becomes the most powerful catalyst in the game for casting Dark Sorceries.

title: Spell Buff
snippet:
Spell Buff -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - overview 
 overview : Upon acquiring a catalyst, be it a Sacred Chime, a Talisman, a Staff, a Pyromancy Flame, or even weapons capable of casting spells (see "Unique Catalysts" for a list of such items), the stat that determines how effective it is at casting is its **Spell Buff**. This number is determined by the amount of Intelligence and Faith of the player (and in the case of one Staff, Luck).

A Staff with 130 Spell Buff will generally outperform one that has 120, if they were to cast the same Sorcery. The same holds true in any catalyst using their appropriate spell, with exception of Dark Spells.

title: Golden Ritual Spear
snippet: As one of the six hybrid catalyst weapons in the game, it is capable of attacking like a spear and casting spells like a staff. However, what makes this weapon so unusual is that while it casts Sorceries, its Spell Buff scales entirely off of Faith. As such, the wielder must level Intelligence solely to meet the weapon's wielding requirements and various Sorceries' casting requirements, while also leveling Faith in order to inflict actual damage with those spells. This means that the wielder must invest heavily into multiple stats simply to use this weapon. Ideally, in order to be efficient as possible Intelligence is only leveled up enough to cast moderately small spells like Great Soul Arrow and Snap Freeze, while the remaining levels are put into Faith to increase their potency.

title: Catalysts
snippet:
Catalysts -  Dark Souls - weapon - usage 
 usage : Catalysts are equipped as weapons and can be used on either the right or left weapon slots. Pressing R1/RB or L1/LB (depending on which side the catalyst is equipped) will cast the selected spell. Depending on the catalyst, pressing R2/RT or L2/LT may result in either a strike or thrust attack.

Each catalyst has a magic adjustment stat that determines the power of the sorceries cast with the catalyst. Magic adjustment affects the damage of sorceries that deal direct damage, and the damage added to weapons by weapon augmentation sorceries. For most catalysts, magic adjustment scales with the caster's intelligence. Exceptions are the Oolacile Catalyst and Oolacile Ivory Catalyst, both of which have static magic adjustment, and the Tin Darkmoon Catalyst, which has magic adjustment that scales with faith instead of intelligence.

title: Sacred Chimes (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Sacred Chimes (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - lead 
 lead : **Sacred Chimes** are catalysts used to cast Miracles. They are primarily differentiated from the other Miracle catalyst, the Talisman, by having generally higher Spell Buff and the skill Gentle Prayer, which gradually heals the wielder over time.

title: Hexes
snippet:
Hexes -  Dark Souls II - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Hexes can be bought from various merchants and trainers, while others can be found as loot throughout Drangleic. Hexes are unique in that they require both Faith and Intelligence in order to be used.

As a general rule, hexes that require more intelligence than Faith require a staff to cast, while those that require more Faith than Intelligence require a sacred chime. Hexes cast from staves tend to be more destructive, while hexes cast from chimes tend to be more passive. In some cases the damage dealt is dependent on the amount of souls the caster has, consuming souls in the process.

Some weapons that are neither staves nor chimes exist which can be used to cast hexes, such as the Mace of the Insolent.

The damage dealt by hexes is heavily influenced by the Dark Attack Bonus stat. Dark bonus is increased as both Intelligence and Faith are raised at the same rate.

title: Priest's Chime (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Priest's Chime (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Priest's Chime is the strongest chime for low to medium Faith builds, and has the lowest requirement of Faith amongst all Miracle-based catalysts, tied only with the Talisman.

Like the Canvas Talisman, the Priest's Chime has a slow Spell Buff growth below 30 Faith, but greatly improves in strength between 30 Faith and 40 Faith before slowing back down. This means that it generally possesses better Spell Buff than almost any other Miracle catalyst at 45 Faith and below, though it ultimately loses to the Cleric's Sacred Chime and Yorshka's Chime past this point.

Although it is weaker than the Rose of Ariandel for much of its range of strength, the Priest's Chime weighs much less, and possesses the Gentle Prayer skill which aids in survivability.

title: Miracle (Dark Souls)
snippet:
Miracle (Dark Souls) -  Dark Souls - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Miracles are cast using talismans as a medium. Talismans scale with the Faith stat, with the unique exception of Velka's Talisman, which scales with the Intelligence.

Most miracles can be purchased from various merchants found throughout the game. Some are found as lootable items or given by various characters.

Miracles are largely utility spells focusing on defensive purposes such as healing, deflecting, and augmentation with few providing pure damage. Unlike sorcery, offensive miracles can deal lightning damage in addition to magic damage.

title: Sorcery (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Sorcery (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Sorcery is cast through staves as a medium and scale with Intelligence.

Some non-staff weapons exist which can be used to cast sorcery as well, such as the Blue Flame and Pilgrim's Spontoon.

Most sorceries can be purchased from various merchants throughout Drangleic. Some sorceries, however, can be found as lootable items on corpses and in chests. Sorcery provides the user with a mix of augmentation and utility, while still giving a wide variety of fully offensive spells which exclusively deal magic damage. The damage dealt by sorceries is influenced by the Magic Attack Bonus stat. Magic bonus is raised with Intelligence.

title: Intelligence (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Staves benefit most from Intelligence investment. The majority of staves will not begin to gain Spell Buff until Intelligence has been leveled past 18. Once past this point though, staves will continue to increase in strength up until the 60 Intelligence mark is reached. In many cases, the rate of improvement will reduce past 45 Intelligence, so this is considered a minor soft-cap for pure Intelligence catalysts.

Dual-scaling catalysts will also benefit from leveling Intelligence, though in a different way, much like their melee analogues. Pyromancy Flames will scale with Intelligence up to 40, alongside Faith. Catalysts that specialize in casting Dark spells like Izalith Staff and Sunless Talisman increase in effectiveness up to 45 Intelligence and 45 Faith. The Crystal Chime, one of the most unique catalysts in the game, also soft-caps at 45 Intelligence and 45 Faith, though it also has a minor soft-cap at 30 Intelligence and 30 Faith.

title: Karmic Justice
snippet:
Karmic Justice -  Dark Souls - spell - general_information 
 general_information : Karmic Justice acts as a sort of auto-defense miracle; it unleashes a powerful shockwave in all directions once it is triggered, dealing damage and knockback to hostiles. The damage dealt by the miracle is dependent on the magic adjust of the weapon in the player's right hand, as well as if they are wearing items like the Crown of Dusk and Red Tearstone Ring. The explosion has a base magic attack power of 300, and is affected by the intelligence and faith scaling of the weapon equipped in your right hand when the explosion occurs.

All weapons have a MagAdjust stat, but it is only visible on weapons that can cast spells. Any weapon that does not have any Intelligence or Faith scaling will have a MagAdjust of 100. Weapons that have Intelligence and/or Faith scaling, such as any Divine weapon, will affect the damage of Karmic Justice.

title: Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Parameter Bonus (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : **Parameter Bonus** (also known as **Scaling**) is a gameplay mechanic in *Dark Souls II* similar to the ones from the first game.

It is a rating ranging from "E" to "S" of how well a weapon synergizes with a specific stat. These stats include Strength, Dexterity, Magic (mainly Intelligence), Lightning (mainly Faith), Fire (mainly a combination of Intelligence and Faith) and Dark (lowest stat between Intelligence and Faith).

All the details are not completely known; in particular, how scaling works when there are multiple stats at once (such as for "quality" weapons).

title: Casting Speed
snippet:
Casting Speed -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - mechanics 
 mechanics : Despite what the menu says, Casting Speed is simply a percentage that multiplies how long the startup of a spell will last. The menu numbers are only usable in so far as telling you what stats can affect natural casting speed.

The menu implies a softcap for casting speed from leveling while it actuality it doesn't exist.

Your natural Casting Speed level is determined by your Attunement, Intelligence and Faith levels, with the formula:

Each Spell has a defined startup duration, which is the part that can be affected by casting speed. Every Spell Casting Tool has a value that multiplies your natural casting speed. Every piece of Casting Gear has a value that multiplies your natural casting.

Your total casting speed is the product of multiplying your natural Casting Speed with each piece of casting gear being used and the Spell Casting Tool that is being used.

title: Magic Barrier (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Magic Barrier (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - spell - effect 
 effect : This miracle casts an aura around its user, causing them to become extra resistant towards Fire, Lightning, Magic and Dark attacks by 150. The duration of this spell depends on Faith and ranges from 70 seconds when spiced down to 10 Faith all the way up to 95 seconds at 34 Faith which caps the duration scaling. In addition, Magic Barrier can affect allied players within a certain radius. This trait is not shared by Great Magic Barrier.

title: Crystal Chime
snippet:
Crystal Chime -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Perhaps the most unique catalyst in the game, the Crystal Chime possesses the properties of both a staff and a chime, allowing it to cast both Sorceries and Miracles.

The chime scales with both Intelligence and Faith, and uses both stats to calculate its Spell Buff when casting Sorceries and Miracles. However, Sorceries and Miracles that do not directly deal damage, such as Heal, the healing effect of Lifehunt Scythe, and Magic Weapon, will only use the Spell Buff gained from their respective stats. If Intelligence and Faith are equal, this will be half of the MagAdjust above 100, such that having 180 MagAdjust would cast Heal as if MagAdjust were only 140.

Due to its high natural MagAdjust at low levels of Intelligence and Faith, it is still stronger than other spell tools for these non-damaging applications before 35 Faith or Intelligence.

title: Tin Darkmoon Catalyst
snippet:
Tin Darkmoon Catalyst -  Dark Souls - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Contrary to all other catalysts, the Tin Darkmoon Catalyst scales with Faith instead of Intelligence, making it useful for Faith builds. Players are still required to meet the minimum intelligence requirement to cast the spell, so it may be more efficient to pair this catalyst with lower intelligence spells that still benefit from magic adjust like the various soul arrows or Great Magic Weapon.

203 magic adjust at 40 faith is very doable, unlike Velka's Talisman which scales a bit worse. This makes the Tin Darkmoon Catalyst superior when planning a build that can use both Sorceries and Miracles. The biggest drawback however is having to kill Gwyndolin, thus not having access to his Covenant until the next game cycle.

title: Attack Rating
snippet:
Attack Rating -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - lead 
 lead : Attack Rating is one of the main factors that determines how much damage weapons do throughout the Dark Souls series.

Attack Rating, commonly abbreviated as AR is a number specific to each Weapon and each element that depends on the weapon, upgrade level, player stats and other equipment that can affect it. This number is used during each attack through a damage formula specific to each game to determine the damage.

title: Elemental Damage
snippet:
Elemental Damage -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Dark Souls III* combines the elemental systems of the previous two games. Hexes no longer exist as their own school of casting, and elemental damage is no longer rigidly locked to how Intelligence and Faith are leveled (for instance, Darkmoon Blade grants Magic damage based purely on Faith).

title: Attunement (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Attunement (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : Attunement determines the number of spell slots the player has available to equip spells, and also increases the player's Cast Speed (this effect is roughly double that of leveling Intelligence or Faith). In addition to these, raising Attunement also increases the number of casts per slot a spell has; however, this varies from spell to spell. Raising Attunement also increases the player's Curse Resist and Agility slightly, and as with every other stat, HP is increased by minute amounts each time.

**20/25/30** are the softcaps for attunement that you’d generally want to stop at for a caster build in terms of spell slots. The caps for attunement are **30/75** for spell slots, **94** for max number of spell casts, and around **50-55** for spell casting speed in conjunction with 50 Faith or Intelligence.

snippet:
Darkmoon Blade (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - spell - effect 
 effect : Reinforces the player's right hand weapon with Darkmoon light, adding 95% of casting talisman/sacred chime's Spell Buff as Magic damage for the next 60 seconds.

Lingering Dragoncrest Ring increases the duration to 78 seconds.

For catalysts that scale with both Intelligence and Faith, such as Caitha's Chime and White Hair Talisman, only the Faith portion of the Spell Buff is accounted for.
